title: Willow and the Lost Nest Fluff
markdown:
One super-duper early morning, before the sun had peeked its head out, Willow the wolf pup already had her ears up, like two fluffy antennae. She let out a big squeaky yawn. Beside her, Thistle the hedgehog did his morning roll and became a perfect pokey ball. High up, in a nest that looked like a fluffy woven cloud, Ember the robin chirped a happy cheep, even though the sunshine was still snoozing.

Something was not quite right.

“My fluff. My precious fluff,” chirped Ember, doing a little flutter-dance. “The softest, warmest, snuggliest bit of my nest lining is gone. Vanished.”

This was not just any fluff. This was the super-special fluff that kept the baby robins, still in their eggs dreaming of worms, perfectly warm. If it was not found, those little eggs would get chilly.

Willow’s ears shot even higher. Her tail gave a determined thump-thump-thump on the dewy grass. “We simply must get it back. Before the sun wakes up properly. It’s still dark enough to be sneaky and silent.”

“Sneaky and silent? My middle name,” Ember chirped, though her bright eyes looked a bit worried.

Thistle, already busy with his tiny magnifying glass (just two dew drops balanced on his nose), peered at the ground. “No time for dawdling, friends. This is important business.”

Off they went. Willow trotted with bouncy-bounce paws. Thistle trundled, prickles wiggling. Ember flitted just above, sharp eyes scanning.

“Look,” Ember squeaked, pointing toward a big tangled briar patch that looked like a giant’s tangled hair. “There’s a clue.”

A bright shiny sparkly blue button.

“A button,” Willow yipped, fluffy tail going whap-whap-whap. For a tiny moment she forgot the nest lining. She bounced right over. Maybe it fell off a giant’s coat. Or a fairy’s tiny waistcoat.

Thistle sighed, a little puff that ruffled his whiskers. “Willow, my dear friend, focus. It’s just a button. The fluff is what matters. The fluffy, warm, baby-robin-saving fluff.”

But Willow was already sniffing. “Hey. Look. Another clue.” A bright red feather snagged on a thorny branch. “This must belong to a super-duper grumpy badger who loves to collect shiny things.” She did a little wobbly wolf-pup dance.

Ember tilted her head. “That feather looks a lot like one of mine. But I didn’t even know I’d lost any feathers this morning.”

Deeper they went into the twisty pokey briar. The air grew thick with the prickly scent of damp earth. Tiny thorns snagged at their fur. They found a smooth grey stone that looked like a tiny sleeping moon. Then a twisty twig shaped exactly like a question mark. Willow’s mind buzzed with lost pirate treasure and secret fairy doors. She was starting to forget why they were even in the briar patch. Adventure felt more exciting than old fluff.

Then Thistle stopped so still you could hear a ladybug tiptoeing. “Wait a minute.” He looked right at Willow. “You have the best nose for sniffing out interesting things, it’s true. But sometimes… don’t you get a little bit sidetracked?”

Willow’s happy ears drooped. Thistle was right. All these shiny twisty things were making her forget Ember and her chilly eggs.

Just then Ember, who had flown a little higher, let out a tiny gasp. “Look.” She pointed toward the very top of the tallest scratchiest bramble.

There it was. The fluffiest, warmest, softest piece of nest lining in the whole wide world, caught on a high branch, looking a little lonely. It had not been stolen by a grumpy badger. It had floated away on the breeze. All those sparkly clues were just random bits the wind had decided to play with.

Willow felt a little blush creep up her furry cheeks. Then her ears perked with purpose. “We need to get that lining back to Ember’s nest, without any delay.”

Willow, biggest and bounciest, scrambled up the lower thicker branches. Thistle, a surprisingly good climber for someone so prickly, scurried after. Ember zipped to the tippy-top. Together they carefully nudged the fluffy lining free. Willow grabbed it ever-so-gently in her mouth, careful not to squish it. They hurried back to Ember’s cozy nest.

Ember tucked the precious fluff into its rightful place. It fit perfectly. “Thank you, my wonderful friends. You saved the day. And the baby robins.”

Willow gave a happy wiggle that shook her whole fluffy body. She had not found a pile of treasure. She had helped her friend, after remembering what the search was for.

And so Willow learned that the brightest clues are not always the ones that glitter, and a friend in need is worth more than a button in a briar.
